questions.q_en: Which of the following is a global network of computing devices?
questions.solution_en:
The Internet is a global network of interconnected computers and computer networks that communicate using standardized protocols (primarily TCP/IP). Unlike the other options, the Internet connects billions of devices worldwide across organizational and geographical boundaries.

· LAN (Local Area Network) connects computers within a limited area like a home, office, or campus.

· WAN (Wide Area Network) connects multiple LANs across larger geographical areas but is typically owned by a single organization.

· Intranet is a private network within an organization that uses internet protocols but is not accessible to the general public.

questions.q_en: What is the role of an Internet Service Provider (ISP)?
options_en: To provide internet access to users
questions.solution_en:
An Internet Service Provider (ISP) is a company that provides individuals, businesses, and organizations with access to the internet. ISPs maintain the infrastructure necessary to connect users to the global internet network, offering services like broadband, DSL, cable, or fiber connections. They act as the gateway between end users and the broader internet.

The other options describe different roles:

· Manufacturing computer hardware is done by companies like Dell, HP, or Apple

· Developing web browsers is done by companies like Google (Chrome) or Mozilla (Firefox)

· Creating websites is done by web developers and designers

questions.q_en: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.solution_en:
Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN (European Organization for Nuclear Research). He developed the first web browser, web server, and wrote the first web pages. He also created the foundational technologies of the web including HTML, HTTP, and URLs. Berners-Lee's vision was for an open platform that would allow information to be shared across the world.

The other individuals mentioned made different contributions to technology:

· Bill Gates founded Microsoft

· Steve Jobs co-founded Apple

· Mark Zuckerberg created Facebook (now Meta)

questions.q_en: Which of the following best describes a dynamic web page?
options_en: A web page that displays the same content for every user and does not change unless manually updated by a developer.
A web page that generates content in real-time based on user interactions, inputs, or data from a database.
A web page that is stored entirely on the user's device and does not require an internet connection to function.
A web page that uses only HTML and CSS without any scripting or server-side processing.
questions.solution_en:
A dynamic web page generates content in real-time based on user interactions, inputs, or data from a database.

Unlike static web pages, which display the same content for every user, dynamic web pages use server-side scripting (e.g., PHP, Python) or client-side scripting (e.g., JavaScript) to deliver personalized or updated content.

Examples include e-commerce product pages, social media feeds, and online banking portals.

· Option (1) describes a static web page.

· Option (3) describes an offline web page or a Progressive Web App (PWA).

· Option (4) describes a basic static web page without dynamic functionality.

questions.q_en: Which part of the URL http://www.example.com/index.html is the domain name?
questions.solution_en:
In the URL http://www.example.com/index.html:

· "http://" is the protocol (Hypertext Transfer Protocol)

· "www" is a subdomain

· "example.com" is the domain name (the unique identifier for a website on the internet)

· "/index.html" is the path to a specific file on the server

The domain name consists of the second-level domain ("example") and the top-level domain (".com"). It's the core part of a web address that identifies a specific website.

questions.q_en:
Select which of the given statement(s) is/are True or False for Downloading and Uploading on the Internet.

(i) Downloading refers to transferring data from a remote server to a local device, while uploading refers to transferring data from a local device to a remote server.

(ii) Uploading is typically faster than downloading because most users consume more data than they share.
questions.solution_en:
Statement (i) is true because downloading involves retrieving data from a remote server to a local device, whereas uploading involves sending data from a local device to a remote server.

Statement (ii) is false because uploading is generally slower than downloading for most users, as internet service providers (ISPs) often allocate more bandwidth for downloading to accommodate higher data consumption. This is known as asymmetric bandwidth allocation, where download speeds are prioritized over upload speeds in most consumer internet plans (asymmetric digital subscriber line or ADSL).

questions.q_en: Which of the following addresses is a Class B address?
questions.solution_en:
IP addresses are categorized into different classes based on their first octet (first set of numbers). For Class B addresses, the first octet ranges from 128 to 191.

· 172.16.12.248 has a first octet of 172, which falls within the range of 128-191, making it a Class B address.

· 10.12.12.248 has a first octet of 10, which falls within the range of 1-126, making it a Class A address.

· 192.168.1.1 has a first octet of 192, which falls within the range of 192-223, making it a Class C address.

· 224.0.0.1 has a first octet of 224, which falls within the range of 224-239, making it a Class D address (used for multicast).

questions.q_en: What does VoIP allow you to do?
options_en: Make voice calls over the Internet
questions.solution_en:
VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) is a technology that allows users to make voice calls using an internet connection instead of a regular (analog) phone line. It converts voice signals into digital data packets that are transmitted over the internet. Services like Skype, Zoom, Google Meet, and business phone systems often use VoIP technology.

VoIP is not primarily designed for the other functions listed:

· Sending text messages (though some VoIP services include this as a secondary feature)

· Sharing files (though some VoIP platforms may include this capability)

· Browsing websites (this is the function of web browsers)

questions.q_en: What is the first page of a website called?
questions.solution_en:
The home page is the main or introductory page of a website that typically serves as the starting point for user navigation. It's the default page that loads when a user visits a website's root domain (e.g., www.example.com without any additional path). The home page generally provides an overview of the website's content, features key navigation elements, and establishes the site's brand identity.

While the terms "main page," "index page," and "front page" might sometimes be used colloquially, "home page" is the standard term in web development and design.

questions.q_en:
Select which of the given statement(s) is/are True or False:

(i) A static webpage is one whose content changes based on the user.

(ii) Basic structure of a web page is created using HTML (HyperText Markup Language) and CSS (Cascaded Style Sheet).
questions.solution_en:
Statement (i) is false: A static webpage is NOT one whose content changes based on the user. Static webpages display the same content for all users and only change when a developer manually updates the code. Dynamic webpages, not static ones, change content based on user interaction or other variables.

Statement (ii) is true: The basic structure of a web page is created using HTML (HyperText Markup Language) and CSS (Cascading Style Sheets). HTML provides the structure and content of the page, while CSS controls the presentation, formatting, and layout.

questions.q_en:
Select which of the given statement(s) is/are correct:

i.A cookie is a text file containing a string of information, which is transferred by the website to the browser when we browse it.

ii.A session cookie is also known as an in-memory cookie or temporary cookie.
questions.solution_en:
Statement i is correct: A cookie is a text file containing a string of information, which is transferred by the website to the browser when we browse it. Cookies store small pieces of data like user preferences, login information, or tracking identifiers.

Statement ii is correct: A session cookie is also known as an in-memory cookie or temporary cookie. Session cookies are deleted when the browser is closed, as they are only stored in temporary memory. They are used to maintain session information for the duration of a user's visit to a website.

questions.q_en:
Select which of the given statement(s) is/are correct about Add-ons and Plug-ins:

(i) Add-ons and plug-ins are the tools that help to extend and modify the functionality of the browser.

(ii) An add-on is a complete program.
questions.solution_en:
Statement (i) is correct: Add-ons and plug-ins are tools that help to extend and modify the functionality of the browser. They enhance browsers with additional features like ad blocking, password management, or specialized content display.

Statement (ii) is incorrect: An add-on is not necessarily a complete program. Add-ons are typically smaller software components that integrate with and extend the functionality of a browser. They depend on the browser to function and cannot run independently. Complete programs, in contrast, can run independently of other software.

questions.q_en:
Choose the correct statement about Domain Name System (DNS):

(i) DNS is a service that does the mapping between domain name and IP address.

(ii) DNS is not required to access a website using URL.
questions.solution_en:
Statement (i) is correct: DNS is a service that does the mapping between domain name and IP address. The Domain Name System acts like a phone book for the internet, translating human-readable domain names (like www.example.com) into machine-readable IP addresses (like 192.0.2.1) that computers use to communicate.

Statement (ii) is incorrect: DNS is required to access a website using URL. When a user enters a URL in a browser, DNS resolution is a crucial step that converts the domain name portion of the URL into an IP address, which is necessary for establishing a connection to the correct web server. Without DNS, users would need to remember numerical IP addresses for every website they want to visit.

questions.q_en: What is the purpose of HTTP?
questions.solution_en:
HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is the foundation of data communication on the World Wide Web. Its primary purpose is to establish the rules for transferring hypertext documents (web pages) that contain links to other resources. When a user clicks on a link in a web browser, HTTP facilitates the retrieval of the linked web page from the server.

HTTP defines how messages are formatted and transmitted, and what actions web servers and browsers should take in response to various commands. It's a request-response protocol in the client-server computing model.
